title: Common-stage additive and shift calculus
statement:
The equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Transport is additive and obeys
$(u_N)_P=u_P$ for $M\subset N\subset P$. The common-stage operations are
representative-independent and make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category.
Every finite diagram of objects, morphisms, composites, and asserted
equalities in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite field, and an
asserted equality holds exactly when it holds after passage to a further
common stage.

Define
$$
 (E,K)[1]=(E,K[1])
$$
and, for $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$, define
$$
 f[1]=\left[M,
 \sigma_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ u[1]\circ\sigma_{M/E,K}\right].
$$
This gives a well-defined additive autoequivalence $[1]$ with inverse
$[-1]$, and every finite-stage inclusion
$j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ commutes with shifts through the
specified comparison.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the ledger's
verified entries contain no filtered-colimit category, and the blueprint
adds the common-stage calculus, in which every finite diagram and every
asserted equality in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite
coefficient field. The nearest entries, each fetched and quoted, are
Definition 4.21.1 ([Tag 00D3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00D3),
the directed-set condition satisfied by the poset $\mathsf{FinExt}_\ell$)
and Lemma 4.21.5 ([Tag 0032](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0032))
with Remark 4.21.6 ([Tag
09P8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P8)). Difference: Stacks
computes the colimit of a diagram in one fixed category, whereas the colimit
here indexes a category, so addition, composition, shifts and finitely many
asserted equalities must first be transported to one common stage.

proof.text: Use the scheme and coefficient hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]: $T$ is noetherian of finite dimension, $\ell$ is invertible on $T$, and stages are finite intermediate extensions of the fixed algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], each $T_{F/E}$ is exact. In [def-weil-triangulated-category], exact means additive between pre-triangulated categories; those categories are additive and have an additive invertible shift. Apply this also at $F=E$, where $T_{E/E}=1$. Thus every $\mathcal C_E(T)$ has Hom abelian groups, bilinear composition, a zero object, binary biproducts, and additive inverse shifts. We use precisely these stated structures, the natural comparisons $\sigma$, and the unit/pentagon and associator-shift coherence supplied by scalar extension.

source.place: Proof, finite-stage additive laws and exact transition functors

proof.text:
For transport write $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$, $A_Y=a_{N,M,F,L}$, $B_X=a_{P,N,E,K}$, $B_Y=a_{P,N,F,L}$, $C_X=a_{P,M,E,K}$, $C_Y=a_{P,M,F,L}$. Put $H=T_{N/M}$, $G=T_{P/N}$, $J=T_{P/M}$, and $b=a_{P,N,M}:GH\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. The pentagon in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] gives $B_XG(A_X)=C_Xb_{T_{M/E}K}$ and the analogous equation for $Y$. Naturality of $b$ gives $b_YGH(u)=J(u)b_X$. Substituting in the transport formula of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] yields
$$ (u_N)_P=B_YG(A_Y)GH(u)G(A_X)^{-1}B_X^{-1}=C_YJ(u)C_X^{-1}=u_P. $$
The unit equations give $u_M=u$. Exact functors are additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category], so each $T_{N/M}$ is additive. Distributivity of composition with fixed associators now gives $(u+v)_N=u_N+v_N$, $0_N=0$, and $(-u)_N=-u_N$.

Reflexivity has witness $M$ since $u_M=u$, and symmetry follows by reversing the equality. If $(M,u)\sim(N,v)$ at $P_1$ and $(N,v)\sim(Q,w)$ at $P_2$, the finite compositum $P=P_1P_2$ exists by the directed-field data in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Transporting both equalities and using step 2 gives $u_P=v_P=w_P$, which witnesses transitivity. No injectivity of the transport maps is assumed.

For two composable arrows at $M$, the transported composite satisfies
$$ v_Nu_N=a_ZT(v)a_Y^{-1}a_YT(u)a_X^{-1}=a_ZT(vu)a_X^{-1}=(vu)_N, $$
and transport of an identity is an identity. If inputs are replaced by equivalent representatives, take the compositum of their equality witnesses and the two proposed operation fields; by step 2 the corresponding inputs coincide there. The displayed identity and additivity then make the outputs of addition, negation and composition coincide there. Thus the operations in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] are independent of the field and representatives. All abelian-group, associativity, identity and bilinearity equations are verified by putting their finitely many representatives over one stage and applying the finite-stage laws established in step 1.

source.place: ## Proof, independence of common-stage operations and category laws

proof.text: There is also a zero object and every binary biproduct, as required by [def-weil-additive-category]. Take $Z=(\Ql,0)$. Scalar extension sends the zero identity to the zero identity, so every transport of $0$ is a zero object; every representative to or from $Z$ is therefore zero. For $X=(E,K)$ and $Y=(F,L)$ choose $M\supseteq E,F$ and take $B=(M,T_{M/E}K\oplus T_{M/F}L)$. Represent the four inclusions and projections at $M$ by the finite-stage ones. The equations $p_ii_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$ hold at $M$, hence on classes by step 4; the identity of $X$ is represented there by the identity of $T_{M/E}K$, and likewise for $Y$. These prove that $B$ is a biproduct. Together with the Hom abelian groups and bilinear composition of step 4, this makes $\mathcal P_T$ additive.

source.place: ## Proof, zero object and binary biproducts

proof.text: For $X=(E,K)$ and $N\supseteq E$ construct $\gamma_{N,X}:X\to(N,T_{N/E}K)$ by the representative $(N,1_{T_{N/E}K})$; the same identity represents a map in the opposite direction. By the unit equations their composites are the two identity classes, so these maps are inverse. For $f=[M,u]:X\to Y$ and $N\supseteq M$, all three maps in $\gamma_{N,Y}f\gamma_{N,X}^{-1}$ are represented at $N$; the outer maps are identities and the middle map is $u_N$. Thus this conjugate is $j_N(u_N)$. This constructs the object identifications mentioned but not defined in the blueprint proof.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-diagram sentence, explicit object identifications

proof.text: For a finite diagram take the compositum of the coefficient fields of its objects and the representative fields of its arrows, and use step 6 to replace every object by its isomorphic scalar extension at this field. By step 4 all specified composites are represented by the corresponding composites there. An asserted equality of parallel composites holds in $\mathcal P_T$ if and only if its two representatives become equal at a further field, by the equivalence relation in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Take the compositum of the witnesses for the finitely many asserted equalities. Step 2 preserves each witness equality at this common field, giving all equations simultaneously. The reverse implication uses that field as a witness for each equality. An empty diagram may use $\Ql$. If just the list of equalities is empty, no witness extension is required: keep the field already containing the diagram's object and arrow fields. Representation of objects is through the displayed isomorphisms, not literal equality of pairs.

source.place: ## Proof, finite diagrams and simultaneous equality detection

proof.text:
Write $s_X=\sigma_{M/E,K}$, $s_Y=\sigma_{M/F,L}$, $h_X=\sigma_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$, $h_Y=\sigma_{N/M,T_{M/F}L}$, and let $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$ and $A'_X=a_{N,M,E,K[1]}$, with analogous notation for $Y$. Associator compatibility of the natural shift comparisons [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] is
$$ \sigma_{N/E,K}A'_X=A_X[1]h_XT_{N/M}(s_X). $$
Naturality gives $h_YT_{N/M}(u[1])=(T_{N/M}u)[1]h_X$. Insert both identities and the transport formula into $S_N(u_N)$, where $S_M(u)=s_Y^{-1}u[1]s_X$; the adjacent inverse comparisons cancel, leaving
$$ S_N(u_N)=A'_YT_{N/M}(S_M(u))(A'_X)^{-1}. $$
Consequently equivalent representatives give equivalent shifted representatives. At a common stage, $S_M(v)S_M(u)=S_M(vu)$ by cancellation of the middle $s_Ys_Y^{-1}$, $S_M(1)=1$, and $S_M(u+v)=S_M(u)+S_M(v)$ by the additive finite-stage shift of step 1. Thus the formula in the statement defines a well-defined additive endofunctor.

source.place: ## Proof, shift well-definedness, explicit compatibility calculation

proof.text:
For inverse shifts use signed reindexing of complexes as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $K[-1][1]=K=K[1][-1]$ and similarly on chain maps. In the derived category these equations are read through the induced natural inverse identifications; all formulas below include them. Put $q_{M/E,K}=(\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]})[-1]:(T_{M/E}K)[-1]\to T_{M/E}(K[-1])$ and $\tau_{M/E,K}=q_{M/E,K}^{-1}$. For $H=T_{N/M}$ put $A_X=a_{N,M,E,K}$ and $A_X^-=a_{N,M,E,K[-1]}$. The positive comparison equation of step 8 at $K[-1]$, shifted by $[-1]$, reads
$$q_{N/E,K}A_X[-1]=A_X^-q_{N/M,(T_{M/E}(K[-1]))[1]}H(\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]})[-1].$$
Naturality of the $H$ comparison, applied to $\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]}$, rewrites its last two factors as $H(q_{M/E,K})q_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$. Consequently, inversion gives
$$\tau_{N/E,K}A_X^-=A_X[-1]\tau_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}H(\tau_{M/E,K}).$$
This derives negative-shift coherence from the cited positive-shift coherence, rather than presupposing it.

source.place: Proof, inverse shift: definition and comparison coherence

proof.text:
For a representative $u:T_{M/E}K\to T_{M/F}L$, define $R_M(u)=\tau_{M/F,L}^{-1}u[-1]\tau_{M/E,K}$. Naturality gives $\tau_{N/M,T_{M/F}L}H(u[-1])=(Hu)[-1]\tau_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$. Write $D_X=\tau_{N/M,T_{M/E}K}$ and similarly for $Y$. Substitute the last equation of step 9 into $R_N(u_N)$ and cancel:
$$\begin{aligned}
R_N(u_N)&=A_Y^-H(\tau_Y)^{-1}D_Y^{-1}(Hu)[-1]D_XH(\tau_X)(A_X^-)^{-1}\\
&=A_Y^-H(\tau_Y^{-1}u[-1]\tau_X)(A_X^-)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is exactly transport of $R_M(u)$ between the negatively shifted endpoints. Equality witnesses therefore remain witnesses after shifting, so $R$ descends to classes. At one stage,
$$R_M(v)R_M(u)=\tau_Z^{-1}v[-1]\tau_Y\tau_Y^{-1}u[-1]\tau_X=R_M(vu),$$
$$R_M(1)=1,\qquad R_M(u+v)=\tau_Y^{-1}(u[-1]+v[-1])\tau_X=R_M(u)+R_M(v).$$
The common-stage descent of step 4 proves that $[-1]$ is an additive endofunctor.

source.place: Proof, inverse shift: representative independence and additive functor laws

proof.text:
Write $S_M(u)=s_Y^{-1}u[1]s_X$ as in step 8, where $s_X=\sigma_{M/E,K}$, and put $t_X=\sigma_{M/E,K[-1]}$; use analogous notation for $Y$. The definition in step 9 gives $\tau_{M/E,K[1]}=(s_X[-1])^{-1}$ and $\tau_{M/E,K}[1]=t_X^{-1}$. Hence
$$R_M(S_M(u))=s_Y[-1](s_Y[-1])^{-1}u\,s_X[-1](s_X[-1])^{-1}=u,$$
$$S_M(R_M(u))=t_Y^{-1}t_Y\,u\,t_X^{-1}t_X=u.$$
These equalities use the signed-reindexing inverse identifications of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Represent their unit and counit at the coefficient field of each object. The displayed calculations at the representative stage of each arrow prove naturality; their triangle composites are the inverse-reindexing identities at that same stage. Thus $[1]$ and $[-1]$ are mutually inverse additive equivalences.

source.place: Proof, inverse shift: inverse functors and natural unit/counit

proof.text: Define $j_E(K)=(E,K)$ and $j_E(u)=[E,u]$. Step 4 proves that these preserve identities, composition and addition. With identity associators normalized, the associator-shift compatibility of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] at $E=M=N$ becomes $\sigma_{E/E,K}=\sigma_{E/E,K}^2$. Its invertibility gives $\sigma_{E/E,K}=1$. The formula of step 8 at $M=E$ therefore yields $j_E(u)[1]=[E,u[1]]$ and the objects agree. This is the specified inclusion-shift comparison (or the same comparison with inverse-reindexing identifications when shifts are presented up to natural isomorphism).

Step 9: q=sigma_{K[-1]}[-1] has the right direction, and the negative coherence is derived from the positive one by naturality of q. Step 10: the R_N(u_N) cancellation checks. Step 11: R S=1 and S R=1 using tau_{K[1]}=(s[-1])^{-1} and tau_K[1]=t^{-1}. Step 12: sigma_{E/E}=sigma_{E/E}^2 forces sigma_{E/E}=1, so j_E commutes strictly with the shift. proof.text:
The relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is reflexive and
symmetric from the definitions, and transitive: if $(M,u)\sim(N,v)$ and
$(N,v)\sim(Q,w)$ with witnesses $P_1,P_2$, transport all to their compositum
$P$, where both equalities hold by the transport formula $(u_N)_P=u_P$ and
the unit/associator equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The same
formula shows that transport is additive and satisfies $(u_N)_P=u_P$ for
$M\subset N\subset P$ (the associator cocycle), so addition, negatives,
identities and composition, computed after transport to one common finite
field, are independent of the representatives and of the field; the
finite-stage additive category laws transported to a common field (with
$T_{F/E}$ additive) make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category. Every finite
diagram is represented over one finite field by transporting objects and
morphisms (via the $\gamma$-isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]), and a finite list of asserted
equalities holds in $\mathcal P_T$ exactly when the transported equalities
hold over a further common stage, by the definition of the equivalence. For
the shift: equivalent representatives define equivalent shifted
representatives by naturality of $\sigma$ and the associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], so $[1]$ and $[-1]$ are well-defined
additive endofunctors, $[1]$ has inverse $[-1]$ (the finite-stage shift
laws), and the inclusion $j_E$ commutes with the shifts through the
specified comparison.
